text: In a touched chunk, an empty range maps its start with mapPos(pos, startSide, mapMode) and is dropped on null (RangeValue.mapMode.B1); the side decides before/after an insertion at the position (RangeValue.startSide.B3).

In a touched chunk, an empty range with startSide != endSide also maps its end with endSide (Simple); it is dropped when the end maps before the start, and when it stays empty with endSide < startSide (RangeValue.endSide.B3, B4).

In a touched chunk, a non-empty range maps from with startSide and to with endSide (Simple mode, never null); it is dropped when newFrom > newTo, or when it collapses to empty and endSide < startSide (RangeValue.endSide.B4); otherwise it is kept, possibly empty. Inclusive ends grow with insertions at them, exclusive ones do not (RangeValue.endSide.B2).

Mapped ranges are re-laid within the chunk: a range that still starts at or after the previous kept end (with sides) is appended; an empty one that falls before it is reinserted at the last earlier slot where it fits, scanning backwards while the earlier range does not start after it; anything else is spilled to a new layer. The new chunk starts at the first mapped range's new from (also when that range is spilled) and holds positions relative to it; its maxPoint is recomputed from the kept points; a chunk with no kept range is removed. Examples: points a(1, startSide 1), b(2, startSide -1) deleting [1,2] -> b, a both at 1 in two layers; [0,3] sides -1/1 with a TrackDel point at 5 (side -1) and a point at 6 (side 0) deleting [3,6] -> the point at 5 is dropped, the point at 6 lands at 3 in a second layer; [0,4]/(point 5) deleting [3,5] -> point at 3 spilled.

`newPos` is set before the keep/spill decision (rangeset.ts:152)
cost: O(r) per range in the worst case (backward scan)

text: Only the unchanged gaps of textDiff (iterGaps) are compared, each with both cursors repositioned at the gap start (old position for the old sets, new position for the new ones); reported positions are new-document positions; differences inside changed text are not reported; when the diff replaces the whole document there is no gap and nothing is reported.

Within a gap, compareRange(pos, end, activeA, activeB) is called for each non-empty stretch outside points whose active non-point values differ (sameValues), e.g. adding mark b [3,9] over mark a [2,4] reports [3,4] with ([a], [a, b]) and [4,9] with ([], [b]).

comparePoint(pos, end, pointA, pointB) is called where either side has a point and the points differ by cmpVal (null for a missing side), or are equal but the active ranges wrapping them (activeForPoint) differ; the stretch is clipped to the gap, so a point spanning a change is reported once per gap ([2,5] and [7,12] for an insertion at 5); empty points are reported as zero-length stretches.

When the comparator has a boundChange method, a non-point stretch whose end differs between the sides, or after which a different number of active ranges continues (openEnd), sets a flag unless that end is the end of the gap; boundChange(pos) is then called at the start of the next non-point stretch, before its compareRange; a point in between clears the flag. Splitting [0,10] into [0,5]+[5,10] (same value) reports only boundChange(5); a boundary at a point reports only the point; with the split exactly at a changed region's edge nothing is reported; without boundChange the same inputs report nothing.

text: span's openStart counts the active ranges that continue from before the stretch: for the first stretch, those that started before `from` (iteration starting at 4 inside [2,5] and [3,8] gives 2); afterwards, how many active ranges of the previous stretch extend past its end (openEnd).

point(from, to, value, active, openStart, index): from is the current position (the iteration start if the point began earlier), to is min(point end, iteration end), active = activeForPoint (ranges of rank >= the point's rank that end after the point, or at its end with endSide >= the point's), openStart = active.length + 1 if the point started before `from`, active.length if its startSide < 0, else min(active.length, open count), and index = the point's set rank. After a point the open count is min(openEnd, active.length).

A point hides everything starting inside it; a non-empty point that ends exactly where the previous point ended is skipped, and empty points at that position are reported: points [2,8] then [8,8] -> both reported; a point [0,4] in a first set and, in a second set, a mark [1,5] and a point [2,4] -> one point [0,4], then span [4,5] with the mark; several empty points at one position are each reported.

The return value is the open count at the end: openEnd of the last stretch, plus 1 when a point continues past `to` (spans(…, 0, 4) inside [2,5] and [3,8] returns 2; a point [2,8] cut at 5 inside a mark [0,10] returns 2; a point ending exactly at `to` adds nothing).
